Parsonage Farm
Primary School
Where children are valued and success is recognised
A very warm welcome to our school! At Parsonage Farm we are incredibly proud of our children and all that they achieve. Our school has a strong family feel where every child is known, valued and encouraged to be the very best they can be. We believe that education is about much more than academic success – it is about developing confident, caring and curious young people who are ready to make a positive difference to the world. Our dedicated staff team work hard to create a nurturing environment where children feel safe, supported and inspired to learn. We hope our website gives you a flavour of what makes our school such a special place to learn and grow.
Sports
We pride ourselves on our strong curricular performance. We aim to challenge our children academically, whilst still providing a strong emphasis on ‘soft-skills’, like communication and relationship building.

Our Vision
Our motto is “Where children are valued and success is recognised”. We strive to create a nurturing environment where every child feels safe, supported and inspired to achieve their best. Our vision is for all pupils to grow into confident, kind and curious learners who are ready to thrive in an ever-changing world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values - Parsonage Farm Primary School
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
Ethos
“Where children are valued and success is recognised”
Values
Our school values are:

Music
Curriculum Intent
‘The sheer joy of music making can feed the soul of a school community, enriching each student while strengthening the shared bonds of support and trust which make a great school.’
Model Music Curriculum (DfE, 2021)
At Parsonage Farm Primary School, our music curriculum aims to provide every child with high-quality music experiences that engage, inspire, and foster a lifelong love and appreciation of music. We provide a broad and engaging curriculum that develops pupils’ musical skills, vocabulary, and creativity. Through listening, performing, composing, and appraising, children explore diverse musical styles and cultures, reflecting our school's inclusivity. We aim to nurture confidence, self-expression, and collaboration while ensuring pupils develop an understanding of the interrelated dimensions of music. Sparkyard Music Curriculum helps us support these key elements through its skills based approach to form the foundation of our music curriculum. We create opportunities to enhance pupils' musical experiences further through regularly KS1 singing assemblies as well as opportunities to participate in local music festivals. We believe these opportunities help develop musicianship, ensemble skills, as well as support performance confidence.
We aim to develop all children’s practical skills while giving them access to a broad range of instruments and musical experiences. Through our curriculum, pupils explore and appreciate a diverse range of musical styles, cultures, and traditions, enabling them to develop confidence, collaboration skills, and a deeper understanding of music as a universal language. This is supported with our ‘Musician of the Month’ where children are able to explore a culture of musical appreciation and understanding.
iRock
We are visited most Friday afternoons by our iRock band coach which is a fee-paying 30 minute music lesson. The iRock programme is designed to be totally inclusive; children can join regardless of their musical experience or ability. All instruments are provided, providing an enriching opportunity that takes the pressure off families. Every week one of our expert band coaches will lead a 30 minute session that happens during the school day. Rehearsals are always fun, exciting a highlight of the school week.
Through consistent band practice, the children develop real-life skills including collaboration, listening, patience, teamwork and initiative. Children in Year 2, 4 and 6 will be able to achieve an entry level qualification with iRock without the anxiety of a formal exam. RSL awards are internationally recognised and an asset to your child’s musical journey.
In 2024, we saw a 99% pass rate across all RSL entrants.
If you're interested visit irock's website.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Breakfast Club
We have a Breakfast Club that runs throughout the school year for all pupils (the club does not run during the school holidays).
The club starts each morning at 7.45am and continues through until 8.45am.
There is a good selection of appropriate activities available for each age group to participate in.
Each child is offered Toast/Cereal and a drink.
At the end of each session the children are escorted to their classroom by the club leader.
If you wish to enquire about a place, please email Miss Gardiner at clubs@pfps.havering.sch.uk
After School Clubs
We run a number of after school clubs, including football, ICT, art and lego.
If you wish to enquire about a place, please email Miss Gardiner at clubs@pfps.havering.sch.uk

PE and Sport Premium
The direct funding for school sport, which was announced by the Government in 2013, provides money directly to Primary Schools to fund improvements to the provision of PE and sport. It is also supportive in helping to build a healthy lifestyle, confidence and a sense of achievement.
PE - School Specifics

Art
Curriculum Intent
At Parsonage Farm we believe that creativity, exploration and freedom of expression are a vital part of childhood development. We encourage children to explore their emotions and express themselves freely through art, developing their cultural, spiritual and moral understanding in a safe and inspirational setting. At Parsonage we value perseverance and hard work; we support children to take risks and challenge themselves, without fear of making mistakes. We believe that our art curriculum provides children with the knowledge, skills, and understanding to create their own works of art and respond to the work of others. We believe our art lessons equip pupils with the ability and confidence to express their individual interests, thoughts and ideas in a respectful way, understanding that what one person views as unattractive, another may view as beautiful and our opinions and perceptions are constantly changing – and that’s what makes art great!
Arts Council

Computing
Curriculum Intent
Our intent for Computing at Parsonage Farm is to deliver a progressive curriculum that builds on prior knowledge, ensuring pupils develop secure foundations and deepen their understanding over time. We aim to equip children with the skills, confidence and resilience needed to thrive in an increasingly digital world. Through the teaching of computational thinking and problem solving, pupils learn to analyse, create, debug and refine programs, encouraging logical reasoning and creativity. Digital literacy is at the heart of our curriculum, enabling children to use technology purposefully, safely and responsibly. Online safety is embedded in a cross-curricular manner, ensuring pupils understand how to protect themselves, recognise risk, and seek support from trusted adults when needed. We also develop awareness of artificial intelligence, helping children understand its uses, benefits and potential risks in age-appropriate ways. To further strengthen our provision, we nurture more-able pupils as Digital Leaders, providing additional training and opportunities to contribute to school life by supporting peers and promoting safe, responsible technology use across the school community.

pageCache.pageTitle: DT & Cooking - Parsonage Farm Primary School
pageCache.text:
DT & Cooking
Curriculum Intent
At Parsonage, we strive to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the design, make, and evaluate process, fostering creativity and innovation. We aim to equip students with the practical skills necessary to create functional products that address real-world needs, while also instilling an appreciation for the contributions of past and current inventors to society and technology. We encourage children to take risks in their learning and use problem solving to find practical solutions. We explore many different areas of Design Technology including; textiles, digital design, cutting, joining, health and safety, product research and cookery. By integrating knowledge of healthy foods and nutrition, we promote overall well-being and encourage cross-curricular links with Science, Technology, Engineering and Maths. These areas instil a lifelong love of learning and a deep curiosity about their environment.
What DT & Cookery looks like at Parsonage Farm...

Geography
Curriculum Intent
Throughout the Geography curriculum at Parsonage Farm, pupils are inspired to develop curiosity and a lasting fascination with both their immediate surroundings in Rainham and the wider world. From Reception to Year 6, learning is carefully sequenced to ensure progression in knowledge, skills and understanding. Children begin by exploring their school environment, gradually extending their awareness to the local community and, by the end of Key Stage 1, securing a clear understanding of the United Kingdom and the countries that make it up.
In Key Stage 2, pupils build upon this foundation to deepen their knowledge of the UK while broadening their perspective to include Europe and, by Year 6, the Americas. Through high-quality teaching of human and physical geography, alongside purposeful fieldwork and engagement with the fieldwork cycle, pupils are equipped to ask perceptive questions, think critically and undertake meaningful enquiry.
We aim to help our pupils appreciate different cultures, communities and landscapes, while also developing a strong sense of responsibility for the world they live in. By the time they leave Parsonage Farm, children have a secure understanding of key geographical concepts and the confidence to see themselves as informed, responsible global citizens.

History
Curriculum Intent
At Parsonage Farm we aim to deliver a high-quality history education that enables pupils to think, act and talk like historians. Our intent is to develop both the disciplinary knowledge and the substantive knowledge required for a rich understanding of Britain’s past and the wider world. We want every pupil to experience history as an active, engaging subject that builds curiosity, cultural capital and a secure sense of chronology.
Key aims
Develop historians: Pupils learn to ask questions, analyse primary and secondary sources, weigh evidence and construct well-founded conclusions.
Build substantive knowledge: Each unit gives pupils coherent factual knowledge about specific periods, societies and themes.
Secure chronological understanding: Topics are taught in chronological order to help pupils place events and developments on a coherent timeline. World history is introduced progressively, with wider global perspectives becoming a focus in upper Key Stage 2.
Local Study: Pupils study the history of Rainham and Parsonage Farm meaningful links between the past and the present.
Engage every learner: Action-packed themed days, practical activities and multi-sensory approaches ensure history is accessible and loved by pupils of all abilities and needs.
Broaden Key Vocabulary in Topics: We explicitly teach historical vocabulary and enquiry skills so pupils can communicate their understanding confidently, encouraging pupils to collate their own vocabulary bank.

Maths
Curriculum Intent
Mathematics sparks curiosity, sharpens thinking and builds resilience. It empowers children to think independently, tackle complex problems and make confident decisions.
At Parsonage, and in line with the White Rose Maths scheme of learning, we are committed to developing resilient mathematicians who enjoy the challenge of problem-solving and understand the relevance of mathematics in everyday life. We deliver engaging, inclusive and accessible lessons that help children not only learn how to solve problems, but also understand the ‘why’ behind the methods.
We develop pupils’ understanding of mathematics through a carefully sequenced, small-steps approach. We help pupils build fluency in key number facts and procedures. We also guide them to reason mathematically by making connections and explaining their thinking. Our curriculum ensures coherence and progression, with each new concept building on prior learning.
We believe that every child can achieve in mathematics and our carefully sequenced teaching allows them to explore concepts using concrete, pictorial and abstract representations, developing deep conceptual understanding before progressing to procedural fluency (first learn the why, then practice the how).
Times tables are a key part of mathematics, providing a foundation for quick and accurate calculations. Fluency in times tables supports problem-solving, reasoning and understanding more complex concepts in mathematics. Our children enjoy practising their times tables, using the Times Tables Rock Stars programme.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) - Parsonage Farm Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Curriculum Intent
Parsonage Farm uses the iLanguages scheme of work and resources to ensure we offer a relevant, inspirational and vibrant French curriculum for KS2. Authentic videos, games and familiar tales are used to teach through 6 themed modules per year, covering the four key language learning skills; listening, speaking, reading and writing.
The scheme was chosen as the learning is clearly cyclical, each unit of each year group revises and builds on previous knowledge, as seen through short and long term plans, and intended to support non-specialist teachers. In so doing, it will always be relevant and in line with meeting national DfE requirements. Grammar, cultural and curriculum links are included in the plans, yet the scheme runs independently of other curriculum areas. Children will be taught how use bilingual dictionaries.
Lessons offer natural opportunities for building Oracy skills, rehearsing and modifying stem sentences and performing through role-play. In addition, we run a yearly French café for Year 4 and a French games afternoon for Year 3 as part of International Week celebrations. Learning a second language offers pupils the opportunity to develop a deeper understanding of self, others and cultural differences. The intention is that the children become problem-solvers, confident communicators and life-long language learners.
What MFL looks like at Parsonage Farm...

pageCache.pageTitle: PE & Sports - Parsonage Farm Primary School
pageCache.text:
PE & Sports
Curriculum Intent
At PFPS we aim to inspire and engage all pupils through a high-quality Physical Education curriculum that fosters a lifelong love of physical activity. We provide all pupils with the knowledge and skills to become physically confident in a way that supports their health and fitness, ensuring they have the chance to take ownership of their own physical well-being and make informed, healthy choices. We recognise that the benefits of being active play a crucial part in children's physical, emotional and mental well-being, and we actively promote positive attitudes towards movement, teamwork and resilience. Through inclusive, challenging and enjoyable experiences, pupils are encouraged to develop competence, cooperation and determination, embedding positive health behaviours into their lifestyle both now and in the future. We also teach pupils to cope positively with both success and failure, developing resilience, sportsmanship and the confidence to learn from every experience. In line with our school values of Where children are valued and success is recognised, we celebrate individual achievement, personal progress and sporting success, ensuring every child feels supported, respected and proud of their accomplishments.
We also offer a variety of clubs and PE lessons that keep children engaged, active, and smiling. Whether it’s learning new skills, working as a team, or simply having fun, sport plays an important role in our school life.
What PE looks like at Parsonage Farm...

RE
Curriculum Intent
At Parsonage Farm, our programme for RE follows the guidelines set out in the 'Agreed Syllabus for Religions Education 2021-26, LB Redbridge & Havering'. Our objectives are to enable pupils to acquire knowledge about and develop an understanding of a diverse array of religions and worldviews. To explore different religious beliefs, values and traditions in order to foster an ability to express their ideas and insights and to combat prejudice, preparing them for adult life, employment and life-long learning.

Science
Curriculum Intent
At Parsonage Farm Primary School, we are committed to inspiring a lifelong love of learning and nurturing an inquisitive approach to the world around us. Our Science curriculum is carefully designed to provide full coverage of the National Curriculum while deepening pupils’ understanding of the natural world and encouraging curiosity through ‘working scientifically’.
Through engaging, hands-on experiences, children develop key enquiry skills including observing over time, carrying out research, identifying patterns and conducting simple experiments. We provide a stimulating, accessible and inclusive learning environment where all pupils can strengthen their understanding across the three main scientific disciplines: Biology, Chemistry and Physics.
